findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body:
`MetricAlertDetectorHandler` used to subclass `DetectorHandler` and implement `evaluate` (returning `[]`). It now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`. It does not implement any of the abstract members: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, or the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`.

`MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` points at this class. So `Detector.detector_handler` (`group_type.detector_handler(self)`) raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class` for any detector of type `metric_alert_fire`.

In `process_detectors` that exception is not caught. It aborts processing for every remaining detector in the list. Before this PR the handler was a harmless no-op.

The abstract methods need stub implementations, or the class should stay a concrete `DetectorHandler` until it is ready. The TODO comment above the class is also now stale.

findings.title: Expected occurrence built with wrong group key in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe
findings.body:
The expected occurrence is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...)`, so its fingerprint is `["<id>:val1"]`. The code under test is called with group key `"group_key"`, so the real `build_occurrence_and_event_data` gives fingerprint `["<id>:group_key"]`.

`IssueOccurrence` and `DetectorEvaluationResult` are dataclasses that compare all fields. The `== expected_result` assertion should therefore fail on the fingerprint mismatch. If it somehow passes, the test is not checking that the occurrence is built for the right group key.

The expected occurrence should be built with `expected_result.group_key` (and value 10).

findings.title: Tests never verify the value passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data
findings.body:
In `test_state_results_multi_group`, `group_2` has value 10, but the expected occurrence is built with value 6. `TestEvaluate` cases do the same: they evaluate with 100 or 8 but build expectations with 6.

These tests only pass because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores `value`. No test checks that the hook gets the actual group value. A regression that passes the wrong value, such as the threshold or another group's value, would go unnoticed.

The mock should encode `value` into the occurrence (for example in `evidence_data`), and the expectations should use the real values.

findings.title: PriorityLevel(new_status) raises for non-standard condition results, aborting the whole packet
findings.body:
`new_status` is computed as `max(DetectorPriorityLevel.OK, evaluation)` over `condition.evaluate_value(value)`. `DataCondition.get_condition_result` can return raw ints that are not valid `DetectorPriorityLevel` members, and it can also return bools or floats.

The new conversion `PriorityLevel(new_status)` raises `ValueError` for any such value, for example `True`→1 or an arbitrary int like 100. The exception propagates out of `evaluate` and `process_detectors`. It aborts evaluation for every group key in the packet and every later detector, with no state committed.

The condition result should be validated or mapped first, or the bad value logged and skipped, instead of crashing.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring for `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` still says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". This PR changed the return type to `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` keyed by group key, so the docstring now misdescribes the contract implementers and callers rely on.
